comment: HTML ONTOLOGY — the IDREF class: the lane's THIRD natively-owned relationship type, and the six types it still does not own, each pinned as a forbids rather than asserted in prose. Measured before it was written (validation/m14/probes/html/construct-probe.mts §1, 1,185 git-tracked documents / 24 repositories): 19 sites, 19 ID tokens, 17 resolvable. A non-zero count is a GAP and not a ruling, which is the same test that overturned `overrides`. The `forbidRelationships` block is the other half of that: a lane that emits none of calls/exports/extends/implements/overrides/instantiates must PIN that, because a differential whose oracle also omits them reports 100% coverage with the omission in its own truth — the shared-premise lesson the lane's own doc records for the bare-`#` hole.

expectRelationships.comment: The anchor itself, positively pinned as `uses` with isInternalAnchor — a >=1 match, so the forbid above is what carries the real weight.

forbidRelationships.comment: An ID token that names no element in this document is NOT a reference and emits nothing. `aria-controls="panel missing-one"` on line 44 is the site; publishing `missing-one` would be a placeholder endpoint in the shape standing rule R7 forbids, and it is the same rule `<label for>` already follows.
`headers` is a table-header reference on `td`/`th` ONLY, per the HTML content model. A `headers` attribute on a `<div>` is not a reference, so the tag-scoped row must not read as a wildcard.

An in-document ANCHOR is `uses`, NOT `references`. `<a href="#panel">` is a navigation carrier in `RESOURCE_RULES` and the lane's ratified label for it is `uses`; `deriveHtmlEdges` derives it as `uses`, so relabelling it would make the differential report the lane's most obviously correct class as MISSING. Pinned as a forbid on the `references` reading so the two classes cannot be silently merged.

NATIVE RULINGS, pinned. `calls`: the pinned tree-sitter-html grammar produces 28 distinct node types across the corpus and NONE is an invocation; the 3,742 `call_expression` nodes all live in inline blocks and belong to the JS delegate, which the seam stamps. A `<form action>` is a navigation the BROWSER performs, which is exactly why it is `uses`.

`exports`: markup has no module surface — 0 of 2 export-ish node types in the grammar, and 0 `export_statement` across 359 inline blocks. The rows an html file DOES publish in this channel are the CSS delegate's and carry `htmlEmbedded`/`embeddedLang`; see html/inline-embedded-code.
`extends` / `implements`: 0 heritage clauses across 9 classes in 359 inline blocks, and no type-declaration node in the html grammar at all.

`overrides`: the falsifiable form is ONE class declaring ONE method name TWICE, not "is there a method". Measured 0 over 9 classes / 67 methods / 359 inline blocks. `method_definition` alone (172 corpus-wide) proves nothing, which is why the probe counts duplicates.

`instantiates`: html has no constructor. 204 `new_expression` nodes across the corpus are all inside inline blocks and are the JS delegate's to filter — it drops the browser globals and keeps 48. The tempting native reading, a kebab-case tag instantiating its custom element definition, is measured at 419 tag instances of which 399 (95.2%) end in an all-digit segment and are compiler code-dump placeholders (`comment-1`, `declaration-12`), not custom elements; the remaining ~20 would be `instantiates` rows in the differential's ALWAYS-COMPARED head that no oracle derives, i.e. fabrication by definition.
